A Caregiver’s hands. A neighbor’s open door. The change happens here.

A brand archetype report & differentiation strategy for Suncoast Center · Where good changes happen.
Brand Archetype Report Identity · Voice · Landscape · Differentiation · Visual Direction · October 2026
What this report is: the result of Suncoast Center’s brand archetype assessment, submitted by Jean Pierre on 14 October 2026, scored with Skyway’s weighted engine across all twelve archetypes, then checked against a team session the same day in which the room re-answered seven of the twelve questions by show of hands. The scores are the engine’s. The reading is ours. Section 02 shows where the two were needed to settle each other.
01 · Brand Identity

The one door in Pinellas that opens for everyone

Eighty-two years into the work, your assessment points somewhere more specific than “compassionate care.” It points to a Caregiver who refuses to triage people out, a neighbor who treats the whole county as the neighborhood, and a quiet belief that people actually change. Caregiver is the unambiguous core. The other two are how the care gets delivered and who it gets delivered to.

Caregiver · The What
Care is the product

A full continuum of behavioral health, from a young child in an early intervention program to an adult with a severe and persistent condition, delivered trauma-informed and recovery-oriented, and open to whoever walks in.

  • Your motto: “Caring for others matters most.” The Caregiver’s, word for word. The room picked it five times.
  • Your character is the Nurse; your character trait is nurturing and compassionate. Six of the team picked the Nurse again.
  • Two of your three strengths are caring and supportive. Your mission verbs are strengthen, protect, restore.
Magician · The How
Change is the promise

Your tagline is not about comfort. It is Where good changes happen: a claim that something will be different on the way out than it was on the way in.

  • Your problem approach: “We transform obstacles into opportunities.” The Magician’s line. Four of the room chose it again.
  • Your first strength is transformative, four hands in the room.
  • You already paint butterflies on the buildings. Metamorphosis is the Magician’s oldest symbol, and you chose it before anyone told you to.
Everyman · The Who
Everyone is the audience

Your stated differentiator is three words long: “We accept everyone.” Your purpose is to connect to others. Your setting is the community center.

  • In the team session, “All people are created equal” tied the Caregiver motto at five hands. It is the Everyman’s creed.
  • The Kind Neighbor took four hands; approachable two; the community center four.
  • You convene sixty people a month from the county’s agencies, schools, government and law enforcement. That is a neighbor hosting the block, not a brand defending a turf.

At the core, you’re a Caregiver.

The Caregiver’s drive is service: to protect people from harm and to be there when nobody else is. Yours shows up in the shape of the organisation itself. You run a sexual assault helpline that answers at three in the morning, a forensic nursing team, a school-based program, crisis intervention and medication management under one roof, and you have done it since 1944 without picking a lane. Most Caregiver brands care for a kind of person. You care for a county. Lean into: presence over promises, the whole continuum as the proof, and “we have been here” as the credential.

Magician and Everyman: your twin influences, each with a job.

The Magician is how you care. “We transform obstacles into opportunities” was your answer to how you solve problems, transformative leads your strengths, and the tagline promises change rather than relief. The Everyman is who you care for. “We accept everyone” is your differentiator, the community center is your setting, and the team session put the Kind Neighbor and “all people are created equal” beside the Nurse. One influence says the door is open to all of Pinellas; the other says something real happens once you are inside. Lean into: the open door as the headline, change as the outcome, and plain neighborly language throughout.

Why the combination is one-of-a-kind.

The twelve archetypes sort into four families by core human drive. Your primary, Caregiver, sits in the Structural family. Your leading family by points is a different one: Connector, which carries 12 of your 37 (Lover 5, Jester 5, Everyman 2) against Structural’s 10. The Magician comes from a third family, Legacy, which holds 9. A Structural core with a Connector center of gravity and a Legacy method is a brand that bridges worlds: it has the institution’s steadiness, the neighbor’s welcome, and the change-maker’s nerve. Your family-fit check fired at 0 of 3, which the engine flags for review. We read it as the bridges-worlds story it usually is, not as an error: the people who run Suncoast Center do not experience it as a structure, even though it is one.

The one thing to make unmistakable
Every provider in the county says it cares. Only one says it takes everyone, and can prove it with the licence, the certification, and the helpline. You are not the most compassionate door in Pinellas. You are the one that never closes.
“Everyone welcome. Good change inside.”
The identity in one line: a Caregiver who takes the whole county, a neighbor who makes it feel like the whole county, and a quiet certainty that people get better here
Read the zeros. Ruler, Creator and Outlaw all scored 0. The Ruler zero is the finding. You are the county’s only CCBHC, its only certified sexual assault center, and the agency that has led its Zero Suicide collective since 2017, and not one answer reached for authority, control, or being in charge. You lead by hosting the room, not by owning it. The brand should do the same: say the credentials as proof of the open door, never as a trophy wall.

The guardrail: Caregiver leads; Magician and Everyman back. Welcome before you treat, and never make anyone earn the door. If a line sounds like an intake form or a miracle, it is the wrong line. You are the place where ordinary people get real care and actually change.

02 · The Archetype Makeup

Caregiver at the heart. Change and welcome in the delivery.

A brand is strongest when it leads with one clear core. Yours is unambiguous: Caregiver at 10 of 37, a full five points clear, which the engine calls a clear primary. Beneath it, three archetypes finished level at 5 apiece, and the engine could not tell them apart. A team session on 14 October did.

Caregiver · Core10
Magician · The How5
Everyman · The Who2

Caregiver 10 · Magician 5 · Everyman 2. The engine recorded a three-way tie for secondary, Magician 5, Lover 5 and Jester 5, and listed them in row order, which is not a result. The Lover and Jester points are the Connector family’s signal: connection, belonging, warmth. When the team re-answered the questions as a room, that signal landed on the Everyman, with Lover taking a single hand. We therefore name Everyman as the second influence on review, and leave Lover and Jester at 5 in the chart where the engine put them. The session decided the order, not the size.

Caregiver · in your words

Your motto, “caring for others matters most,” your character, the Nurse, your trait, nurturing and compassionate, and two of your three strengths, caring and supportive. Four answers, one archetype, and the room repeated three of them.

Magician · how you work

You solve problems by transforming obstacles into opportunities. Your first strength is transformative. Your tagline promises that good changes happen here. And the butterflies on the buildings were there before this report was.

Everyman · who you are for

Your purpose is to connect to others, your setting is the community center, your differentiator is “we accept everyone.” In the room, “all people are created equal” and the Kind Neighbor arrived together.

The whole brand, in one line

Your tagline: “Where good changes happen.” The Magician’s promise, made by a Caregiver, to everyone. The word doing the quiet work is where: a place, open, in Pinellas, for eighty-two years.

03 · Core Purpose

So nobody in Pinellas has to earn their way to getting better

Suncoast Center exists so that a young child, a teenager with anxiety, a parent at the end of their rope, an adult with a condition that has followed them for decades, a survivor in the first hour after an assault, and a person who has decided tonight is the night, all have the same door, and the same answer when they knock. The county has providers for each of those people. You are the provider for all of them, and the one that will not ask which they are before letting them in. The purpose is not comfort. It is the change that happens once the door is open: strengthen, protect, restore, in that order, for a healthy community.

It is the Caregiver’s purpose, to be there for everyone who needs us, delivered the Magician’s way: with the expectation that people change, and the Everyman’s way: with no one turned away.

Alternates to react to

Every age. Every challenge. One door, and it is open.

Eighty years of good changes, and we are still here for the next one.

04 · Voice & Personality

Speak like the nurse who lives down the street.

If the brand were a person: a nurse who has worked in Pinellas for thirty years, knows which bus gets you to Largo, has every other agency’s director in her phone, and answers it at two in the morning. She calls you by your first name, never asks what you can pay before she asks what happened, and tells you plainly what comes next. She has seen people get better, which is why she expects you to.

Welcoming

We are open, plain-spoken, first-name  ·  not gatekeeping, eligibility-first, or intake-form cold.
“You don’t need a referral, a diagnosis, or a reason. You need to come in.”

Caring

We are present, patient, every-step-of-the-way  ·  not pitying, saccharine, or pamphlet-speak.
“Whatever brought you here, we’ve helped someone through it before. We’ll help you through it too.”

Transformative

We are certain people change, specific about how  ·  not miracle-speak, toxic positivity, or vague hope.
“Six months ago she couldn’t get her son to school. Last week she chaired the parent group.”

Straight

We are honest, trauma-informed, backed by data  ·  not clinical jargon, false reassurance, or anything that could be mistaken for misinformation.
“Here is what the first visit looks like, what it costs, and what we’ll ask you. No surprises.”

On the dials: neighbor over institution · plain over clinical · calm over urgent · specific over inspirational · warm but never soft on the truth · proud of the credentials, quiet about them.

Front-door line

“Every age. Every challenge. One door. If you live in Pinellas, it’s open to you.”

Funder or partner line

“The county’s only CCBHC, its only certified sexual assault center, and the agency that convenes the rest. When you fund us, you fund the whole system of care.”

Social post

“We’ve been answering the phone in Pinellas since 1944. The number still works. The door’s still open.”

The guardrail: the warmth comes from being there, never from adjectives. If a sentence needs the word “compassionate” to sound compassionate, it is the wrong sentence. Every competitor in the county already owns that word.
Part II · The Strategy

Now that we know who you are, here’s how you win.

The identity only matters if it opens a lane the competition can’t follow you into. So we mapped the behavioral health market around Pinellas County, the agencies you named and the platforms your clients see on their phones, and looked for the gap that only a Caregiver with an open door and a change to promise can fill.

05 · Competitive Landscape

Three camps. None of them own your lane.

Behavioral health in Pinellas sorts into three camps: the county nonprofits you sit beside at the Workgroup table, the health systems for whom behavioral health is one line on a long menu, and the national apps. Every one of them says it cares. (Read from each brand’s public positioning on 14 October 2026, scoped to Pinellas and the Tampa Bay region; to be validated with the client on review. A deeper teardown can follow.)

Camp One
The county peers
WhoDirections for Living, Boley Centers, Operation PAR, and the other partners of the Wellness Connection Our readCaregiver + Innocent. Each has a specialty: family and housing, mental disability and housing, substance use VoiceCompassionate and hopeful; “life gets better here,” “better tomorrows,” “there is hope” You winThey each hold a corner of the county; you hold the whole continuum. They promise hope, a feeling. You promise change, an event, and you take everyone who comes.
Camp Two
The health systems
WhoEvara Health, BayCare Behavioral Health, Windmoor, and the hospital-based programs Our readCaregiver + Ruler. Scale, scheduling, service lines, “comprehensive care for every stage of life” VoiceInstitutional and reassuring; portals, service menus, accreditation logos You winFor them behavioral health is one card on the menu; for you it is the whole house. A patient does not have to find the right department. There is only the one door.
Camp Three
The apps
WhoBetterHelp, Talkspace, and the subscription-therapy platforms advertising into Tampa Bay Our readEveryman + Magician. Convenience, matching, “start today,” a therapist in your pocket VoiceFriendly and frictionless; app-store language, pricing tiers, testimonials in sans-serif You winAn app can see you on Tuesday. It cannot see your child at school, answer in the first hour after an assault, or run a suicide-prevention pathway across a county. You do all of that, and you have telehealth too.
The open lane
One organisation that is all three at once: as warm as the peers, as complete as the systems, as easy to walk into as an app.

The peers can’t cover the whole continuum, the systems can’t make behavioral health the whole building, and the apps can’t be in the room. Nobody else in Pinellas holds the only CCBHC, the only certified sexual assault center, and the Zero Suicide chair at the same time, and nobody else says “we accept everyone” as the first line rather than the fine print. That is the lane, and it is empty.

06 · Differentiation Strategy

Five ways to pull away

Each pillar targets the open lane, and each is something the brand should actively say, not just imply.

Make “everyone” the front door, literally.

Every competitor’s site opens with a feeling: hope, better tomorrows, life gets better. None opens with a promise about who is allowed in. Your differentiator is three words long and none of them is an adjective: we accept everyone. Any age, any challenge, any ability to pay. That is a claim no specialist can make and no health system will lead with, and it is the first thing a frightened person needs to hear.

In the brandPut the open door above the fold on every surface: the homepage, the helpline card, the door itself. “Every age. Every challenge. One door.” Stop leading with “compassionate care”; the category already owns it.

Say the three onlys as proof of the door, not as a trophy wall.

The only CCBHC in the county. The only certified sexual assault center. The agency that has chaired Zero Suicide Partners of Pinellas since 2017. Each is a fact a competitor cannot repeat, and today they sit in a paragraph beneath a list of accreditation logos. Your Ruler zero says you will never want to brag about them, which is right. So frame each one as the reason the door can stay open: the CCBHC model is why nobody is turned away for the wrong insurance; the certification is why the phone is answered at three in the morning.

In the brandOne sentence each, in plain English, on the about page and in every funder deck: what the credential lets you do for a person, never what it says about you.

Promise change, not hope.

The county speaks the Innocent’s language: hope, tomorrow, better. It is honest and it is soft. Your tagline is the Magician’s: where good changes happen. Change is an event with a before and an after, and your CCBHC data can show the after. The butterflies on the buildings already say this; the words have not caught up with the paint.

In the brandTell before-and-after stories with a time stamp and a number. Carry “Where good changes happen” onto the helpline card, the email signature and the impact report cover. Retire “your path to healing starts here”; a path is a hope, a change is a result.

Be the neighbor who hosts the block.

Sixty people from the county’s agencies, the schools, government and law enforcement sit in your room every month because you asked them to in 2017. The Wellness Connection and Zero Suicide Partners both came out of that room. That is the Kind Neighbor the team chose, at county scale, and it is the one thing none of the three camps can claim: the peers attend, the systems send a representative, the apps are not invited. Convening is a brand act. Treat it like one.

In the brandName the room publicly, show the partners’ logos as guests rather than rivals, and let the Workgroup be a line in the brand story. “No wrong door” is your phrase already; make it yours out loud.

Give funders the same door as clients.

Your audience splits in two: the people who walk in, and the partners, sponsors, donors and grant-makers who keep the door open. Most agencies run two brands for them, warm for clients, institutional for funders. Your Caregiver core and Sage receipts let you run one. A grant officer wants to know the money reaches everyone and that outcomes are measured; that is the open door and the CCBHC data, the same story told with numbers.

In the brandOne voice, two proofs. Client-facing surfaces lead with the door and follow with a change story; funder-facing surfaces lead with the change data and follow with the door. Never a separate corporate register.

Your strategic sweet spot
The Caregiver with the open door.

The whole continuum, for the whole county, with the certainty that good changes happen once someone walks in.

07 · Visual Identity · Concept Strategies

Three ways to look the part

Direction, not decoration: three strategic concepts for the brand’s visual identity, each true to Caregiver × Magician × Everyman and each built from the three colours you chose. We’ll design the boards once a direction is picked; this is the thinking the boards will rest on.

Concept A
The open house

The welcome mat, designed.

Everyman-forward. A warm sand field with cobalt type and a single marigold accent, photographed in real Pinellas rooms rather than stock. Signage that reads like a front porch, type that reads like a neighbor talking. The door is the recurring device: open, lit, at every size.

Pros
  • Says “we accept everyone” before a word is read
  • Lowest barrier for stigma-sensitive and first-time clients
  • Warmest foil to the health systems’ white-and-blue
Tradeoffs
  • Underplays the Magician; can feel like a community center and nothing more
  • Weakest in a funder deck beside institutional peers
Concept B
Metamorphosis

Good changes, made visible.

Magician-forward, and the only concept that keeps the butterflies. The existing butterfly is refined into a mark system that carries a cobalt-to-marigold light gradient, the dawn in the painting. Motion, before-and-after storytelling, and the tagline as the brand’s spine. Sand as the quiet ground beneath it.

Pros
  • Owns the one idea no competitor in the county has: change, not hope
  • Builds on an asset already on the buildings and in the community’s memory
  • Ownable; nobody in any camp looks like this
Tradeoffs
  • Butterflies are a crowded symbol in healthcare; the refinement has to be rigorous
  • Gradients need discipline in print and on signage
Concept C
Civic modern

The trusted institution, lightly worn.

Your “Modern / Sleek” pick, taken at its word. Cobalt and white, a confident grid, a sturdy serif for headlines, marigold as a thin rule. The look of a public institution people trust with the county’s hardest work, cleaner and brighter than the navy you asked us to avoid.

Pros
  • Strongest with grant-makers, government and the Workgroup table
  • Ages well; easy to govern across a large organisation
  • Reads as the CCBHC it is
Tradeoffs
  • Drifts toward the health-system look you need to escape
  • Underplays the Everyman; cobalt-and-white can feel like a portal, not a porch

The color thinking

You chose cobalt, marigold and sand, and you ruled out crimson, navy and tangerine. The rulings are as useful as the picks. Crimson in a brand that runs forensic nursing reads as blood and emergency, and it is right to keep it out. Navy is what every institution in the county already wears, and ruling it out says you want to look awake. Cobalt is a Caregiver colour, trust and calm, and it is also the sector default; on its own it will not separate you from the health systems. Marigold is the differentiator: it is the Magician’s light, and no county peer leads with a warm yellow. Sand is the colour that makes the other two work. Two checks the client cannot get elsewhere. First, cobalt and marigold together is a flag palette: Sweden, Ukraine since 2022, IKEA, and locally the Rays’ navy-and-yellow. Never set marigold type on a cobalt field at scale, and never use the two as a flat 50/50; keep sand as the field, cobalt as the voice, marigold as light (a gradient, a glow, the butterfly’s wing). Second, marigold sits beside amber on hazard signage. Keep it off the crisis and helpline interfaces, where cobalt should carry the whole job, so the warm colour never says “warning” to a person in crisis. Your gradient pick, teal into green, confirms the instinct toward light moving across a surface; our recommendation is to make that gradient cobalt into marigold and let it live in the mark alone.

The type thinking

You chose “sturdy and characterful”: a serif with weight and personality, confident, a little crafted. That is the right voice for a Caregiver who has been here since 1944 and does not need to shout, and it gives the Magician somewhere to live. Fraunces is the lead recommendation: a variable serif with real weight at display sizes and a soft axis that keeps it warm rather than stern; Lora is the quieter alternative if the organisation wants fewer moving parts. Pair it with a humanist sans for everything a person has to read quickly: Nunito Sans for the warmest read, Archivo if the Modern / Sleek pick should show in the body. The Everyman rule for the system: nothing a nervous person has to squint at. Generous sizes, short line lengths, and the serif only where there is room for it to breathe.

Our lean: Concept B, executed with Concept A’s warmth. A metamorphosis system that refines the butterfly you already own, carries the cobalt-to-marigold light in the mark, and sets it all on a sand field that reads as a front porch rather than a portal. It is the only direction that says all three things at once: everyone is welcome, we have been here, and good changes happen inside.
08 · Summary

A Caregiver brand with a neighbor’s door and a magician’s promise.

The whole continuum, for the whole county, delivered by people who are certain that good changes happen. In a market where every agency claims compassion, every system has a menu, and every app has a tier, you are the one door in Pinellas that opens for everyone and means it.

What you told us.

Every answer from the assessment, unedited, followed by the team session tally. The report is our reading of these; this is the record they were read from.

The business
Describe what you do
Suncoast Center has been serving the residents of Pinellas County since 1944, remaining steadfast in our mission to strengthen, protect, and restore lives for a healthy community. At the forefront of this mission, Suncoast Center provides a full spectrum of services designed to meet the needs of individuals across all ages and address the entire range of behavioral health challenges. Implementing the Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) model, we are committed to delivering integrated, trauma-informed and recovery oriented care that is both accessible and tailored to the unique needs of each person we serve.

Our services span the entire continuum of care, from early intervention and prevention programs for young children to specialized treatment for adults facing severe and persistent mental health conditions. We offer individual and group therapy, medication management, crisis intervention, and substance use treatment, all deeply rooted in trauma-informed practices that prioritize the dignity, safety, and well-being of every client. Our multidisciplinary team, including experts in early childhood development, mental illness, and substance use disorders, ensures that our care is informed by the latest research and best practices, delivered with the highest standards of compassion and respect.

In response to the evolving needs of our community, Suncoast Center has expanded its range of services to provide even more support to families and individuals. For families with children, we offer early childhood services, school-based services, in-home parenting support, and family therapy, all designed to strengthen family dynamics and promote healthy development. These expanded services also include specialized care for adolescents, addressing issues such as anxiety, depression, and behavioral challenges with age-appropriate, trauma-informed interventions. For adults, we provide enhanced support for those managing complex mental health conditions, with a focus on recovery-oriented care that empowers individuals to reclaim their lives and thrive.

Suncoast Center is Pinellas County’s Sexual Assault Services Center, certified through the Florida Council Against Sexual Violence. Our team of specially trained forensic nurses, advocates, and trauma therapists work to treat those who need help processing, coping and navigating through their recovery process. We provide immediate crisis intervention, forensic evidence collection, mental health and trauma therapy services, support and peer groups, and advocacy to sexual violence survivors, all delivered with a trauma-informed approach that honors each survivor’s journey toward healing.

Moreover, our outreach and educational programs include workshops, support groups, and community initiatives that address the broader social determinants of health, contributing to the creation of a more resilient and informed community.

By offering a full range of services that address every stage of life and every behavioral health challenge, and by expanding our offerings through the CCBHC model and trauma-informed care, we are fulfilling our commitment to leading the way in behavioral health and wellness. Our comprehensive, compassionate care is designed to support every member of our community in their journey toward a healthier, more vibrant future.

Leading the Way in Behavioral Health and Wellness
Suncoast Center believes in quality data informed treatment and practices using the Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic model. We have been awarded a Substance Abuse Mental Health Services Administration CCBHC grant and our attestation has been accepted by SAMHSA. We are accredited through the Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities (CARF) International. We are Pinellas County Sexual Assault Center certified through the Florida Council Against Sexual Violence. We are licensed to provide outpatient Substance Abuse services through the Department of Children and Families.

Read Our 2025-2026 Impact Report
Community Collaboration
Suncoast Center values collaborations and serves as a leader in collaboration for behavioral health services. Suncoast Center initiated and has led our Pinellas County Behavioral Health System of Care Workgroup since 2017. Every month we convene both behavioral health agencies and collaborative partners including schools, government entities, law enforcement representatives, to collaborate and inform on existing services and partnerships, and to identify and address areas for improvement and improved collaboration. We routinely have attendance of 60 people at our collaborative meetings. Out of this collaboration has emerged the Wellness Connection and the Zero Suicide Partners of Pinellas.

The Wellness Connection is an entity that ties together the partners of Suncoast Center, Boley Centers, Operation PAR, PEMHS, Directions for Living, Baycare Behavioral Health, Evara Health, Windmoor, and Central Florida Behavioral Health Network. The partners are directly addressing and improving access to care for individuals in need of behavioral health services. The Wellness Connection is addressing a no wrong door approach to services and effective collaboration and care coordination across sectors.

The Zero Suicide Partners of Pinellas was initiated as a collective impact project of the Pinellas Behavioral Health System of Care Workgroup in 2017. It has been continuously led by Suncoast Center since its inception. The project first assisted agencies and providers to initiate a common suicide prevention screening and treatment care pathway that is evidence based within each agency site. The project has brought training and cross training across partners increasing understanding and collaboration. The project is now addressing outreach activities for outreach and calls to action that address prevention in keeping with SAMHSA’ National Strategy for Suicide Prevention, the CDC’s Preventing Suicide: Technical Package of Policy, Programs, and Practices; and the U.S Playbook to address Social Determinants of Health from the Domestic Policy Council Office of Science and Technology. Please visit our Zero Suicide Partners of Pinellas website to learn more and become involved.
